title: Package of Practices for Rice Blast Management in Eastern & Central India
organization: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack
state: Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh
content: Rice blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia grisea) attacks leaves, nodes, and panicles. Symptoms include spindle-shaped lesions with grayish centres and brown margins. Leaf blast occurs during tillering under high humidity (>90%) and night temperatures (20-24°C). IPM Recommendations: 1) Cultural: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer (>100 kg N/ha in blast-prone areas); apply nitrogen in 3-4 split doses. Maintain optimal field drainage. 2) Biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5-10 g/kg seed. 3) Chemical (if disease severity crosses 5% leaf area): Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L (120 g/acre in 200 L water) OR Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L OR Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2.0-2.5 ml/L. Pre-harvest Interval (PHI) for Tricyclazole is 30 days. Spray during calm morning hours with safety protective gear.

title: Soil-Test Based Integrated Nutrient Management for Irrigated Rice
organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad
content: Recommended standard N:P2O5:K2O ratio for high-yielding varieties is 100:50:50 to 120:60:60 kg/ha (approx. 40-48 kg N, 20-24 kg P2O5, 20-24 kg K2O per acre). Application timing: 1) Basal: 25% Nitrogen + 100% Phosphorus (DAP/SSP) + 50% Potash (MOP) at transplanting/puddling. 2) Active Tillering (20-25 DAT): 50% Nitrogen as top dressing. 3) Panicle Initiation (40-45 DAT): Remaining 25% Nitrogen + 50% Potash. Zinc deficiency correction: Apply Zinc Sulphate heptahydrate (21% Zn) @ 10 kg/acre basal or foliar spray of ZnSO4 (0.5%) + 0.25% lime at 30 DAT if deficiency symptoms (khaira disease) appear.

title: Integrated Management of Yellow (Stripe) and Brown Rust of Wheat in Indo-Gangetic Plains
organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal
state: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar
content: Yellow rust (Puccinia striiformis) appears as bright yellow powdery stripes of uredinia parallel to leaf veins during cool, humid weather (10-15°C). Brown/Leaf rust (Puccinia triticina) appears as scattered orange-brown pustules. Management: 1) Grow resistant varieties like HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-222, DBW-303, PBW-725. 2) Early detection: Inspect fields weekly during December-February. 3) Chemical intervention: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (e.g. Tilt) @ 1.0 ml/L (200 ml in 200 L water/acre) OR Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.0 ml/L at first appearance of stripe rust pustules. Repeat after 15 days only if rust progresses. Do not delay spraying once yellow streaks appear.

title: Irrigation and Fertilizer Schedule for Timely Sown Wheat
source_type: State Agricultural University Package of Practices
content: Fertilizer dose for medium soil: 50 kg N (110 kg Urea), 25 kg P2O5 (55 kg DAP), 12 kg K2O (20 kg MOP) per acre. Apply all DAP, MOP, and 1/2 Urea at sowing. Apply remaining 1/2 Urea with first irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage (20-25 DAS). Critical Irrigation Stages (5-6 irrigations): 1) Crown Root Initiation (21 DAS - critical), 2) Tillering (40-45 DAS), 3) Jointing (60-65 DAS), 4) Flowering/Booting (80-85 DAS), 5) Milking (100-105 DAS), 6) Dough stage (115-120 DAS). Avoid irrigation during high winds at grain filling to prevent lodging.

title: Management of Pink Bollworm and Sucking Pests in Cotton
organization: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur
state: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana
content: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) damages flowers ('rosette flower' symptom) and green bolls, causing stained lint and seed destruction. Sucking pests (Jassids, Whitefly, Thrips) cause leaf curling and honey-dew secretion. IPM Strategy: 1) Install Pheromone Traps @ 2 traps/acre for monitoring and 8-10 traps/acre for mass trapping at 45 DAS. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days or 10% rosette flowers or 10% damaged green bolls. 2) Release Trichogramma bactrae @ 60,000 parasitized eggs/acre/week starting from 45 DAS (3-4 releases). 3) Spray Neem Oil (1500 ppm) @ 5 ml/L at early squaring. 4) Chemical Spray at ETL: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L (60 ml/acre) OR Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5 g/L (100 g/acre) OR Profenofos 50% EC @ 2 ml/L (400 ml/acre). For Whitefly at ETL (6-8 adults/leaf): Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 2 ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L.

title: Integrated Management of Black Thrips (Thrips parvispinus) and Leaf Curl in Chilli
organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru
state: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Odisha
content: Thrips parvispinus feeds heavily on flowers, flower buds, and young foliage, causing flower drop, scarred fruits, and upward leaf curling ('boat shape'). Thrips also vector Chilli Leaf Curl Virus. IPM Strategy: 1) Cultural: Install Blue and Yellow sticky traps @ 20-25 traps/acre at canopy height for mass trapping. Plant barrier crops (2-3 rows of Maize or Sorghum around the field). 2) Botanical/Bio: Spray Neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2 ml/L or Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5 g/L. 3) Chemical (alternate modes of action): Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 1.0 ml/L (200 ml/acre) OR Fipronil 5% SC @ 2.0 ml/L (400 ml/acre) OR Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD @ 1.2 ml/L. Do not repeat the same chemical consecutively to prevent resistance buildup. Add surfactant/sticker (0.5 ml/L) for better coverage.

title: Early Blight and Late Blight Management in Tomato
organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi
content: Early Blight (Alternaria solani) shows dark brown concentric target-board ('bullseye') spots on older leaves. Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) shows water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips and margins with white downy fungal growth on underside under cool, foggy, humid conditions. Management: 1) Prophylactic/Preventive: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L (500 g/acre) OR Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5-3.0 g/L at early vegetative stage. 2) Curative for Late Blight: Spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L (500 g/acre) OR Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil MZ) @ 2.5 g/L OR Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L. Repeat at 7-10 day intervals during persistent cloudy/humid weather. Observe 7-10 days PHI before harvesting.

title: Management of White Rust and Sclerotinia Rot in Rapeseed-Mustard
organization: ICAR - Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR), Bharatpur
state: Rajasthan, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, UP, West Bengal
content: White rust (Albugo candida) causes white or creamy-yellow pustules on lower leaf surface and severe staghead hypertrophy of floral parts. Sclerotinia stem rot causes water-soaked lesions on stems with white cottony mycelium and black sclerotia. Management: 1) Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35% WS (Apron) @ 6 g/kg seed. 2) Sowing time: Sowing between 10th-25th October significantly reduces disease incidence. 3) Foliar spray: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g/L (400-500 g/acre) OR Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at 50-60 DAS upon seeing first pustules. Repeat after 15 days if cloudy weather persists.

title: Integrated Pest Management of Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) in Chickpea and Pigeonpea
organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur
state: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh
content: Gram pod borer larvae chew round holes in green pods and feed on developing seeds with their body half inside. Management: 1) Install bird perches @ 15-20 per acre for natural predatory birds. 2) Install pheromone traps @ 2-3 traps/acre for monitoring (ETL: 1 larva/meter row or 5-6 moths/trap/day). 3) Bio-pesticides: Spray HaNPV (Helicoverpa armigera Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) @ 250 LE/acre (1.5 ml/L) in evening hours with 0.1% jaggery as UV protectant OR Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L. 4) Chemical Spray: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L (60 ml/acre in 200 L water) OR Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4-0.5 g/L (80-100 g/acre) OR Indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 1.0 ml/L. Spray during early larval instars (1st-3rd instar) for maximum efficacy.

title: Management and Reclamation of Saline and Sodic Soils in India
organization: ICAR - Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal
state: Haryana, Punjab, UP, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu
content: Distinction between Saline and Alkali/Sodic Soils: 1) Saline Soils: EC > 4 dS/m, pH < 8.5, ESP < 15. Reclamation: Leaching with good quality irrigation water followed by subsurface drainage. Gypsum is NOT required for pure saline soils. Grow salt-tolerant varieties (e.g. CSR-36, CSR-43 in Rice; KRL-210, KRL-213 in Wheat). 2) Sodic/Alkali Soils: pH > 8.5, ESP > 15, EC variable. Reclamation: Apply agricultural-grade Mineral Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) based on Gypsum Requirement (GR test). Broadcast gypsum uniformly in summer, mix in upper 10 cm soil, pond water for 10-15 days. Green manuring with Sesbania (Dhaincha) @ 20 kg seed/acre incorporated at 45 days markedly improves organic carbon and infiltration rate.

title: Drip Irrigation and Fertigation Scheduling for Horticultural Crops
state: Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra
content: Drip fertigation saves 40-50% water and 25-30% fertilizer while increasing crop yield by 20-35%. Water-soluble fertilizers (WSF) like 19:19:19, 12:61:0 (MAP), 0:0:50 (SOP), 13:0:45 (Potassium Nitrate), and Urea are recommended. Application Guidelines: 1) Vegetative Stage: High Nitrogen and balanced Phosphorus (e.g. 19:19:19 + Urea). 2) Flowering & Fruit Set Stage: High Phosphorus for root and flower development (12:61:0 + 19:19:19). 3) Fruit Development & Maturation: High Potassium (0:0:50 / 13:0:45) for fruit size, color, firmness, and shelf-life. Never mix Calcium Nitrate with Sulphate or Phosphate fertilizers in the same fertigation tank to prevent insoluble precipitation. Flush lateral pipes with plain water for 10-15 minutes after each fertigation cycle.
